title: Building Self-Improving Agent Software Factories — Suraj Gupta, Warp
talk_summary: Warp's Harness lead describes three concrete self-improvement loops for agent factories: an outer-loop agent that rewrites inner-loop skills via PRs, per-agent persistent memory stores that capture facts/learnings from past runs, and rule-based model routing backed by best-at-k evals.

takeaways.technique: Outer-loop agent that rewrites inner-loop skills via PR
takeaways.what_they_do: A separate agent observes the inner agent's runs plus human feedback signals (thumbs, comments, employee replies), synthesizes improvements, edits the skill file, and opens a PR so a human reviews the change before it takes effect.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we added the triage skill, and then we open a pull request... a human is actually going to review those updates to the skill

takeaways.technique: Per-agent versioned fact store with source provenance
takeaways.what_they_do: An outer-loop agent extracts facts/learnings/outcomes from inner-loop runs into a memory store scoped to that agent; memories are versioned, human-editable, traceable to the source run, and reported back as 'memories used' on later runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can think of this as a fact store scoped to an agent... future runs of the agent can lean on what's already been done in the past

takeaways.technique: Task-class routing rules plus best-at-k eval sidecar
takeaways.what_they_do: Routing is expressed as rules mapping task classes to models (e.g. migrations to GLM, docs to Qwen), and an eval sidecar runs the same prompt across several models best-at-k to decide which model actually wins per task class, rather than trusting generic benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do this with a simple like best-at-k um approach where when you type a prompt, we run a bunch of agents in Oz uh across a different set of models

takeaways.what_they_do: They are building evals where users define what they care about per task class and test routing configurations against their own workflows instead of public benchmarks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: is Haiku better than fi- than GLM than Opus in a specific class of issues? That's like specific to your workflows and not just some like generic benchmark

takeaways.technique: Inner/outer loop separation as a standing role
takeaways.what_they_do: They formalize two roles: inner-loop agents do the work, outer-loop agents only observe runs and feedback and improve the inner loop's artifacts (skills, memory). The outer loop is a scheduled workflow, not ad hoc.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your inner loop agent is the thing that's actually applying the skill... you have this other outer loop agent that is observing your inner loop agent's runs
